text.p: National Societe Generale Bank will propose to shareholders issuing non-convertible Egyptian pound floating-rate bonds with a maturity of five years, a bank official said on Sunday.
"The interest will be above the average yield on three-month T-bills," added NSGB investment manager Tareq Fayed.
"The yield on T-bills will be our reference, but if that is not available, bond rates will be minus (at a discount on) the Egyptian Central Bank's discount rate,"he told Reuters.
The bank has already said it is proposing to issue the bonds up to an amount of 150 million pounds ($44 million).
It will put the proposal to an extraordinary general assembly of shareholders on February 13.

"We can not say how much the premium will be right now, but it will be within the range of prevailing market rates," Fayed added. Other recent Egyptian bank bond issues have been at 0.25 percentage points above the yield on six-month treasury bills, which now stands at 10.041 percent.
French bank Societe Generale has held a majority stake in National Societe Generale since last October.
